docs.title: readme
docs.text:
keyboard-first terminal client for imessage, slack and telegram, in one chat list.

imessage goes through a bluebubbles-compatible server; slack and telegram talk to their own servers directly. all of them render the same way, and which backend owns a conversation is never something you have to think about.

== contents ==

  quick start          get it running
  configuration        settings, env vars, theme
  slack                tokens, what works, what does not
  telegram             logging in, what works, what does not
  using it             keys, composer commands, chat list
  behaviour            link previews, emoticons, chat management
  development          layout, checks, troubleshooting

== quick start ==

  requirements
    go 1.25 or newer
    for imessage: a bluebubbles-compatible server, over http and websocket
    slack tokens, if you want slack -- optional, see below
    a telegram login, if you want telegram -- optional, see below

  every network is optional; the app needs one. a bluebubbles server that
  is configured but unreachable at startup is reported in the status line
  and left out until the next start, so it never keeps slack or telegram
  from loading. one that answers but does not hand over its chat list in
  time (15 seconds) is asked again after 5s, 15s, 30s, a minute, then every
  two minutes; the status line says so, and its panes keep their chats from
  the cache until the list arrives.
  with nothing configured at all, the app says so on stderr and exits.

  build and run
    go build -o imessage-tui .
    export BB_SERVER_URL=https://your-server:1234
    export BB_PASSWORD=your-api-password
    ./imessage-tui

  the tui owns the terminal, so nothing is ever printed to stdout.
  runtime logs go to ~/.imessage-tui.log -- read that first when something
  looks wrong.

== features ==

  chat
    imessage, slack and telegram in one list, searchable, with unread markers
    optimistic sending: your message appears at once and reconciles later
    tapbacks, slack and telegram reactions render as compact emoji on the
    message
    thread replies, quoted replies, image attachments, link previews
    slack threads inline in the channel, or in a pane of their own with /t
    urls open with a click on the url itself, or with /open

  layout
    up to 8 panes, split horizontally or vertically, each with its own chat
    up to 9 tabs, each its own set of panes -- slack in one, imessage in
    another
    per-pane focus, resizable dividers, resizable chat list
    layout, ui state and message cache survive a restart

  reading
    sender names get a stable colour per person, so a busy channel can be
    read by who is talking. shown in group chats and hidden in one-to-one
    chats by default; ctrl+b flips a single chat and is remembered
    optional timestamps, line numbers, sender names, pane dividers, previews

  connection
    realtime over websocket (imessage), socket mode (slack) and mtproto
    updates with gap recovery (telegram)
    api polling reconciles anything the realtime feed missed
    a backend that is down costs only itself

== configuration ==

  read from env vars and ~/.config/imessage-tui/imessage.yaml; env wins.
  credentials prefer the os keyring and fall back to the config file.
  ui state, layout, message cache and per-chat overrides -- aliases, pins,
  ignores, sender-name choices -- live in ~/.config/imessage-tui/

  setting                   env var                     default   what it does
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  server_url                BB_SERVER_URL               unset     bluebubbles url
  password                  BB_PASSWORD                 unset     api password
  theme                     BB_THEME                    auto      auto|light|dark
  notifications             BB_NOTIFICATIONS            off       off|bell|desktop
  message_limit             BB_MESSAGE_LIMIT            50        messages per chat
  chat_limit                BB_CHAT_LIMIT               50        imessage chats listed
  poll_interval_sec         BB_POLL_INTERVAL_SEC        10        refresh; 0 disables
  enable_link_previews      BB_ENABLE_LINK_PREVIEWS     true      preview metadata
  max_previews_per_message  BB_MAX_PREVIEWS_PER_MESSAGE 2         previews per message
  preview_proxy_url         BB_PREVIEW_PROXY_URL        empty     optional json proxy
  oembed_endpoint           BB_OEMBED_ENDPOINT          noembed   oembed endpoint

  env only
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  BB_INSECURE_TLS           unset     skip tls verification (self-signed; insecure)
  BB_SLACK_TOKEN            unset     slack user token, one workspace
  BB_SLACK_APP_TOKEN        unset     slack app-level token, for realtime
  BB_SLACK_WORKSPACE        slack     label for the env workspace

  chat_limit applies to imessage and telegram (at most 100 there, one page
  of dialogs). it means "the most recent N", which needs a list ordered by
  recency; slack's is not, so every slack conversation is fetched rather
  than an arbitrary slice of them.

  for imessage it counts known senders: the N most recent chats with people,
  plus up to N more from unknown senders (what messages files under Unknown
  Senders -- banks, deliveries, one-time codes), which the list keeps out of
  the way. chats with no messages left are not listed: that is what a
  conversation deleted on the phone looks like to bluebubbles, since its
  messages move to Recently Deleted but the chat itself stays.

# ~/.config/imessage-tui/imessage.yaml
server_url: "https://your-server:1234"
password: "your-api-password"
theme: auto
notifications: off
message_limit: 50
chat_limit: 50
poll_interval_sec: 10
enable_link_previews: true
max_previews_per_message: 2

== theme ==

  auto keeps a compromise palette. every colour is chosen to stay readable on
  light and dark alike, and message text carries no colour at all so it
  inherits the terminal's own foreground.

  pinning dark or light additionally tunes the palette for that background:
  on dark the accent blue, timestamps, dividers and sender colours brighten,
  since they no longer have to survive a white background too.

  auto never picks the tuned palette. background detection queries the
  terminal over stdin, multiplexers answer it themselves, and a wrong guess
  paints unreadable text -- a conservative palette is the better failure.

  on a black-background xterm: set theme: dark, and make sure TERM is
  xterm-256color. a TERM without a colour suffix makes lipgloss strip every
  colour, so the palette never gets a chance.

== notifications ==

  off by default. inside the app a message always gets noticed: see
  "chat list and status". this setting is for when the terminal itself is
  out of sight.

  bell       rings the terminal bell. terminals and window managers turn
             that into an urgency hint, tmux flags the window, and over ssh
             it is the one that reaches the machine in front of you.
  desktop    a desktop notification: notify-send on linux (mako, dunst,
             gnome, kde), osascript on macos.

  either goes out only while the terminal window is not focused, which the
  app learns by asking the terminal for focus reports. a terminal that never
  sends any -- tmux needs `set -g focus-events on` -- is treated as watched,
  and is alerted only for chats that are not on screen. a chat rings or
  notifies once per 30 seconds however many messages it sends, and ignored
  chats, your own messages, and unknown senders while those are hidden never
  do.

== slack ==

  slack conversations appear in the same chat list as imessage. nothing about
  it goes in imessage.yaml: slack is on when tokens are present and off when
  they are not, and the app starts either way. a workspace that fails to
  connect costs that workspace only.

  two tokens per workspace, because slack needs two
    xoxp-...   user token: the web api acts as you and sees what you see
    xapp-...   app-level token: opens socket mode, and nothing else

  fastest way in, for one workspace
    export BB_SLACK_TOKEN=xoxp-...
    export BB_SLACK_APP_TOKEN=xapp-...
    export BB_SLACK_WORKSPACE=acme     # optional label

  for several workspaces, or to keep tokens out of your shell profile, put
  them in the os keyring. an existing ~/.slack_config.json is imported on
  first run and the log says so -- delete that file afterwards, it holds both
  tokens in plaintext.

  what works
    channels, private channels, dms, group dms
    threads. the replies to the ten newest are shown inline in the channel,
    marked ↳, in time order among everything else. /t #N opens a thread in
    a pane beside the channel -- the root, then every reply in order --
    where anything you send posts in the thread. /r #N answers in a thread
    from the channel itself
    files, opened with /img #N or a click
    reactions, mentions resolved to names, emoji shortcodes
    messages from apps -- alertmanager, linear, ci bots: their attachments
    and block kit layouts are drawn as text, title, body, fields and links,
    each attachment with its colour bar beside it
    *bold* _italic_ ~strike~ `code`, ```code blocks``` and > quotes, drawn
    as styles with the marks taken out
    realtime over socket mode, several workspaces at once

  what does not
    deleting or renaming a conversation. imessage-only; the app says so
    rather than pretending
    marking read without a write scope on the user token (channels:write,
    groups:write, im:write, mpim:write). without it slack answers
    missing_scope, the app stops asking for that workspace, and everything
    else keeps working
    channels you have not joined, archived channels, closed dms. the list is
    your membership, the same thing slack's own sidebar shows
    a thread's read state. slack's web api has no call for it, so a thread
    pane marks nothing read
    an app's buttons, menus and inputs, which only do something inside
    slack. a button that opens a url shows as that link; the rest are left
    out. tables and slack's link-unfurl cards are not drawn

  ordering
    imessage first, then each workspace: people and group chats before
    channels, alphabetically. slack's conversation list carries no
    last-activity timestamp, and getting one would cost a history call per
    conversation, so recency ordering is not on offer.
    with more than one workspace connected, names are prefixed with the
    workspace so two "#general" stay apart -- in pane headers, toasts and
    the plain recent list. the chat list leaves it out where a group header
    or the network filter already names the workspace.

  if conversations are missing, the log says what was fetched
    grep "conversations" ~/.imessage-tui.log

== telegram ==

  telegram chats appear in the same list, most recently active first, as in
  telegram itself. like slack it needs nothing in imessage.yaml: it is on for
  every account that is logged in.

  log in once, before starting the app
    imessage-tui telegram login           scan the qr code: telegram on the
                                          phone → settings → devices → link
                                          desktop device
    imessage-tui telegram login --phone   a code to the telegram app or sms
                                          instead
  a two-step verification password is asked for when the account has one.

  telegram wants an api id and hash of your own, from https://my.telegram.org
  → api development tools. login reads BB_TELEGRAM_API_ID and
  BB_TELEGRAM_API_HASH (or TG_API_ID / TG_API_HASH, as the desktop app
  does), asks for them otherwise, and stores them with the session. after
  that a normal start needs no environment.

  the session is the login itself -- whoever has it is you -- so it lives in
  the os keyring, never in a file. it shows up in telegram's device list as
  imessage-tui.

    imessage-tui telegram accounts        what is logged in
    imessage-tui telegram logout [<id>]   end the session on telegram's side
                                          too, and forget it

  what works
    private chats, groups, supergroups, channels, saved messages
    replies (/r #N), reactions, photos and files (/img #N), stickers as their
    emoji, unread counts, marking read
    realtime with gap recovery, several accounts at once

  what does not
    secret chats. they are end-to-end encrypted to one device and do not
    exist for a second client
    deleting or renaming a chat, sending files. edits made elsewhere do show
    formatting: bold, italics and labelled links arrive beside the text and
    are drawn plain

  reactions: telegram has no ‼️ or ❓, so emphasize and question send 🔥
  and 🤔. a chat can restrict reactions further; the error says so.

== keys ==

  single-letter shortcuts (? q d r g G /) and the plain arrow keys only act
  when you are not typing. with the composer or chat search focused they edit
  text instead. anything using ctrl, alt or shift works everywhere, including
  mid-message.

  moving around
    tab                    switch focus between chat list and panes
    esc                    back to the chat list
    up / down, k / j       navigate chats, or scroll messages
    g / G                  top / bottom of the chat list; in a pane, G and
                           end both jump to the newest message
    pgup / pgdown          scroll the focused pane
    /                      search the chat list
    n / N                  filter the chat list to the next / previous
                           network: all, imessage, each slack workspace
    s                      group the chat list by network, or back to recent
    p                      pin or unpin the selected chat
    K / J                  move a pinned chat up / down in Pinned
    x                      ignore the selected chat, or stop ignoring it
    I                      show or hide ignored chats
    U                      show or hide chats from unknown senders
    t                      show or hide the time on each chat list row
    enter                  open the selected chat, or send the composer
    shift+enter            newline in the composer
    ? / F1                 help
    q / ctrl+c             quit

  panes
    ctrl+f                 split the focused pane left and right
    ctrl+g                 split the focused pane top and bottom
    ctrl+w                 close the focused pane
    shift+left / right     move between panes, also while writing
    ctrl+up / ctrl+down    move to the pane above or below
    ctrl+shift+left/right  resize the focused split
    ctrl+left / ctrl+right resize the chat list

  tabs
    alt+t                  new tab, with one empty pane
    alt+w                  close the tab; its chats stay in the list
    alt+1 ... alt+9        go to tab N
    alt+, / alt+.          previous / next tab
    alt+r                  name the tab; an empty name goes back to naming
                           it after its networks
    alt+n                  go to the newest unread chat

  toggles
    ctrl+s                 chat list
    ctrl+t                 timestamps
    ctrl+n                 line numbers
    ctrl+e                 pane dividers
    ctrl+p                 chat previews in the list
    ctrl+b                 sender names for this chat, remembered
    alt+m                  sender names in one-to-one chats too

  chat actions
    d, then D              delete the selected chat, esc cancels
    r                      rename the selected chat
    ctrl+d / ctrl+r        the same two, from a pane
    ctrl+o                 pin or unpin the chat in the focused pane

  mouse
    click to focus a pane, open an image or open a url where it is drawn,
    double-click a chat in the list to open it in the focused pane,
    click a network chip to filter the chat list, click a tab on the tab bar
    to show it, click the unread badge to open the list on that chat, scroll
    to move through history,
    drag the chat list edge or a pane divider to resize.

== composer commands ==

  typed into the message box and sent with enter, instead of the message.
  the #N is the row number shown by ctrl+n.

    /r #N text    reply to row N. on slack this posts into that message's
                  thread -- the same thread when row N is itself a reply.
                  on imessage it becomes a quoted reply
    /t #N         open the thread on row N in a pane beside this one, or
                  focus the pane already showing it. slack only; anything
                  sent in that pane posts in the thread
    /img #N       open the image on row N
    /open         open the newest link in the pane
    /open #N [K]  open link K on row N, counted in the order they are
                  drawn; K defaults to 1
    /h            react to the newest message with a heart
    /lol          react with laughing
    /tu           react with thumbs up
    /te           react with thumbs down
    /!!           react with emphasis
    /?            react with a question mark

  on slack the six reactions map onto :heart: :joy: :+1: :-1: :bangbang:
  :question:

== chat list and status ==

  there is no persistent status bar. prompts you have to act on -- delete and
  rename confirmations, errors, toasts -- appear on the bottom row while they
  are live, then disappear.

  unread chats are marked in the chat list and with a dot on pane headers.
  a pane you are looking at clears its own marker.

  a message for a chat that is nowhere on screen -- in no pane of the tab
  shown, and not in the list, because it is hidden or filtered to another
  network -- shows as a toast on the bottom row: chat, sender, text. with
  the list hidden, the top-right corner names the newest unread chat and
  counts the rest (● Family +2); clicking it opens the list on that chat.
  alt+n goes to the newest unread chat from anywhere: to the pane already
  showing it, in another tab if need be, or else into the focused pane.

  with more than one tab open, a tab bar sits above the panes: each tab's
  number, then its name -- the one given with alt+r, or else the networks
  its panes show, so a tab of slack channels reads as that workspace without
  being named -- and a dot while a pane in it holds a message you have not
  seen. a single tab has no bar. going to a tab filters the chat list to
  its network, or to all of them when its panes mix networks; an empty tab
  leaves the filter as it was. panes in a background tab keep taking
  realtime messages; the periodic reload covers only the tab on screen, and
  a tab coming back reloads whatever went stale while it was hidden. the
  8-pane limit is per tab. tabs, their names and their panes survive a
  restart.

  with more than one network connected, a row of chips under the title --
  All, iMessage, each slack workspace -- picks which the list shows: click
  one, or step through them with n and N. a chip with unread chats shows how
  many. clicking a network's header in the grouped list filters to it too. s
  groups the list under a header per network, imessage first, then slack
  workspaces in config order; within a group a chat with a new message still
  moves to the top. filter and grouping combine with / search, and both are
  remembered across restarts.

  ctrl+p shows the last message under each chat. a chat with nothing to show
  -- every slack conversation, since slack's list carries no last message --
  stays on one line rather than leaving an empty one; with previews off every
  chat is one line. the choice is remembered.

  p pins the selected chat to a Pinned section at the top of the list, in
  both sort orders, and ctrl+o does the same from a pane. pinned chats keep
  the order you give them -- new pins go last, K and J move one -- rather than
  moving with each new message, and still answer to the network filter and
  search. pins live in chat_overrides.json beside the local aliases.

  x ignores the selected chat: it leaves the list, the Pinned section and
  every unread count, and stays gone when new messages arrive. this is local
  to the app -- nothing is deleted or muted on the phone. I shows ignored
  chats in an Ignored section at the bottom, where x on one brings it back.
  ignores are kept in chat_overrides.json too.

  chats from unknown senders are hidden unless they have a new message, which
  lists them among the others so a code that just arrived can be found. U
  shows all of them in an Unknown senders section near the bottom; pin one
  to keep it in view.

  deleting a chat with d needs the bluebubbles private api. without it the
  delete fails and the chat comes back; x is the way to get rid of it here.

== behaviour ==

  emoticons
    the composer rewrites text emoticons as emoji. an emoticon has to stand
    as its own whitespace-delimited word, so "hej :)" converts and
    "http://x" does not

      <3 </3 :) :-) =) :( ;) :| :* 8) :'( \o/   convert as you type
      :D :P :p :O :o xD XD :/ :\ B) o/          convert on the next space

    the second group waits for a word boundary so ":Down" and "xDrive"
    survive and urls keep their "://". a rewrite is skipped while the cursor
    sits behind the end of the text, so editing earlier in a draft never
    moves you to the end.

  sender names
    shown in group chats, hidden in one-to-one chats. a group is a chat whose
    participants say so (imessage), or a pane where more than one other
    person has written (slack channels, telegram groups). alt+m shows names
    in one-to-one chats too.
    ctrl+b flips the chat in the focused pane, in every pane showing it, and
    is remembered in chat_overrides.json. flipping it back to what the chat
    would show anyway forgets the choice, so it follows alt+m again.

  links
    a url in a message opens in the browser when you click the url itself --
    clicking elsewhere on the message only focuses the pane -- including a
    long url broken across rows. a preview line opens from anywhere on it.
    /open opens the newest link in the pane, /open #N [K] the K-th on row N.
    only http and https links are ever opened.

  link previews
    supported media urls render a compact preview line

      [YouTube] video title        [Spotify] track or playlist title
      [Instagram] post or reel     [Aftonbladet] article title

    hosts: youtube.com m.youtube.com youtu.be spotify.com open.spotify.com
    instagram.com m.instagram.com aftonbladet.se expressen.se dn.se svd.se
    svt.se omni.se gp.se sydsvenskan.se di.se

    fetches are async: a fallback label first, then the metadata. html
    metadata is preferred, so generic titles like "search" are ignored and
    refetched.

  emoji
    shortcodes are decoded from the same table the composer autocompletes
    from, generated from the dataset slack itself uses -- so :saluting_face:
    arrives as an emoji rather than as text, and anything you can receive is
    something you can type with ":".
    workspace-custom emoji have no unicode character and stay as their name.

  chat management
    delete uses the bluebubbles private api and clears the local cache only
    after the server confirms: d, then D, esc to cancel.
    rename uses the group-rename api when available; if the server rejects
    it, the alias is saved in chat_overrides.json and applied on refresh.

== development ==

  layout
    main.go              startup: config, backends, theme, bubble tea
    provider/            the seam between the ui and the chat backends
    provider/imessage/   adapts api/ and ws/ to it
    provider/slack/      slack web api, socket mode, mrkdwn, guids
    provider/telegram/   telegram over mtproto (gotd/td), login, updates
    termqr/              qr codes drawn in the terminal, for logins
    emojiset/            the shared shortcode table, generated
    api/                 bluebubbles http client, contacts, attachments
    ws/                  socket.io/websocket client, reconnect + overflow
    config/              config, credentials, ui/layout/cache state
    models/              chat, message, attachment, link preview
    tui/                 models, split layout, rendering, input, persistence

    conversations are addressed by guid, and which backend owns one is
    derived from its prefix: unprefixed is imessage, sl: is slack, tg: is
    telegram. nothing outside provider/ parses a guid.

  checks
    go test ./...
    gofmt -l .
    go vet ./...
    go build ./...

    the tui tests run with a throwaway HOME, so they never touch the layout,
    ui state or chat overrides in your own ~/.config/imessage-tui.

  docs
    the root *.md files are the source of truth. scripts/docs.sh stages them
    into docs/ for mkdocs, and docs/*.md is gitignored, so never edit there.
    AGENTS.md has the rules that are easy to get wrong in this codebase.
    SLACK.md has the slack design and its known limits; TELEGRAM.md and
    SIGNAL.md do the same for telegram and for signal, which is planned.

== bluebubbles setup ==

  the server must run on a mac signed into icloud with messages enabled.
  grant it full disk access, accessibility and automation.

  verify connectivity with the same url and password the app uses

    curl -k "https://your-server/api/v1/server/info?password=YOUR_PASSWORD"

== troubleshooting ==

  no colour at all
    check TERM. a value without a colour suffix, such as rxvt or plain
    xterm, makes lipgloss strip every escape sequence. use xterm-256color.

  tls errors
    verify url, certificate trust and password. certificates are verified by
    default; for a self-signed server set BB_INSECURE_TLS=1, which is
    insecure and env-only on purpose.

  missing contact names
    make sure contacts are available to bluebubbles itself.

  stale chats
    check websocket connectivity. polling reconciles open chats when enabled.

  slack conversations missing
    grep "conversations" ~/.imessage-tui.log for what was actually fetched.
    0 dm usually means the token lacks im:read.

  telegram missing
    grep telegram ~/.imessage-tui.log. "no longer authorized" means the
    session was ended from another device: log in again.

  anything else
    ~/.imessage-tui.log has it. the tui never writes to the terminal.
